faq.q: How do I choose a trusted grown-up?
faq.a: Pick someone who listens to you, makes you feel safe, and helps when you need it. A trusted grown-up never asks you to keep secrets that make you feel worried or unsafe.

faq.q: What does a school counsellor do?
faq.a: A school counsellor is trained to listen and help children with worries, feelings, friendships and problems at home or school. You can ask your teacher how to see them.
It is a free phone or online chat service where trained, kind people listen to children. Many countries have one, such as Childline in the UK or CHILDLINE 1098 in India.
asks: Is there a number I can call for help?

faq.q: What if the grown-up I tell does not help?
faq.a: Keep telling other trusted grown-ups until someone helps. You deserve to be listened to and kept safe.
asks: What if nobody listens to me?

faq.q: What if someone asks me to keep a secret that worries me?
faq.a: Happy surprises, like a birthday present, are fine to keep. But a secret that makes you feel worried, scared or unsafe should always be told to a trusted grown-up.
asks: Should I keep a bad secret?

facts: Childline, a free helpline for children in the UK, was started in 1986 by TV presenter Esther Rantzen.
Child Helpline International links children's helplines in more than 130 countries around the world.
